To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

polyethyleni-mine-grafted CNTs are prepared by grafting polyethyleneimine (PEl) onto the surface of NH2–MW NTs, which are obtained by introducing car-boxylic acid groups to the surface of pristine MWNTs.
polyethyleniminemultiwalled carbon nanohybrids have been prepared by grafting polyethylenime onto the surface of amine-functionalised multiwalled carbon nano-tubes.

we have prepared polyethyleni- mine-grafted multi-walled carbon nanotube (PEI-g-MW NT) hybrids by grafting polyethylenimi ne onto the surface of amine-functional- ized MWNTs through two mechanisms, activated monomer mechanism and activated chain mechanism, by which protonated monomers or the termini of growing chains are transferred to the amines on MWNTs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a noncovalent approach for the immobilization of DNA on the surface of C60 and CNTs.
the preparation of PEI-g- MWNTs by a grafting-from method.
the development of a new type of CNT-DNA complex that is suitable for gene delivery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PEI-g-MWNs are a promising material for the noncovalent and secure immobilization of DNA and the efficient delivery of DNA.

PEI-grafted MWNTs can be used to immobilize DNA securely onto the surface through electrostatic interactions, which are much stronger than the noncovalent interaction between DNA and pristine MWNTs or other CNTs functionalized with nonionic groups, such as carboxylic acids.
the functionalization of CNTs with PEI provides a secure and efficient way to immobilize DNA and to deliver DNA to cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have prepared a new type of CNTs that can be used for efficient and secure immobilization of DNA.
we have successfully prepared polyethyleniminemultiwalled carbon nanohybrid by grafting PEI onto NH2-MWNTs.
the noncovalent functionalization of MWNTs with PEI is a simple and efficient approach for immobilization of DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PEI-g-MWTNs are promising candidates for nonviral gene delivery because of their high transfection efficiency and the secure immobilization of DNA.
PEI-g-MWTs are promising candidates for the delivery of DNA and other biomolecules.
PEI-g-MWTs are a new type of nanomaterial that can be used for the noncovalent, secure, and efficient immobilization and delivery of DNA.
